evidence.detail: `node bin/speckiwi prd coverage docs/prd/2026-11-04.v530-wave-master-work-graph-roadmap.prd.md --target 5.3.0 --json` reports ungroundedCriteria for 8 new criteria: FR-NODE-245 AC-3, FR-NODE-251 AC-7, FR-NODE-253 AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, FR-FLOW-211 AC-4, FR-FLOW-213 AC-2, FR-FLOW-216 AC-4. Cause, from src/core/prd/coverage.ts:104-106 and :146-150: a Rationale is split into segments only at line breaks and `;`, and the reason after `fills: PRD-<n> / <kind> /` runs to the end of the segment, so an `AC-n ← PRD-m` written after a fills clause in the same sentence-run paragraph is read as prose. Each affected Rationale (50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:16431, :16805, :16925; 60.workflow-release.srs.md:14727, :14852, :15019) puts a `fills:` clause before later AC citations separated only by `. `.

findings.req_id: FR-NODE-245, FR-NODE-251, FR-NODE-253, FR-FLOW-211, FR-FLOW-213, FR-FLOW-216
findings.description: Eight acceptance criteria that do cite a PRD item (or carry a fills basis) are reported by the shipped PRD coverage tool as having neither, because a preceding fills clause in the same Rationale segment swallows their citation. PRD coverage and the computed wave PRD items (FR-FLOW-219 AC-1, IR-CLI-114 AC-2) would read these criteria as ungrounded.
findings.suggested_action: End each `fills: ... / <reason>` clause with `;` or a line break in these six Rationale paragraphs (or move fills clauses after the plain citations), then rerun `speckiwi prd coverage ... --target 5.3.0 --json` until ungroundedCriteria is empty. Consider adding the segment rule to FR-FLOW-209 so kiwi-srs prescribes it.

evidence.detail: 60.workflow-release.srs.md:15209 (FR-FLOW-219 AC-2): "AFTER the initial authoring and after each incremental authoring, THE host SHALL run `speckiwi prd coverage --target <product target>`, and an intent, goal or in-scope item it reports uncovered SHALL stop the run before the next dispatch." vs docs/prd/2026-11-04.v530-wave-master-work-graph-roadmap.prd.md:328-336 (PRD-27, confirmed in-scope proposal): "로드맵은 다음 target 으로 나눠 이어서 구현한다". Tool output for this very PRD and target: `prd coverage ... --target 5.3.0` lists PRD-25 (in-scope), PRD-26 (in-scope) and PRD-27 in uncitedItems.

findings.description: A PRD whose in-scope items are deliberately split across targets (this run's own PRD) leaves those items uncovered by the product target, so FR-FLOW-219 AC-2 stops every wave-master run of 5.3.0 before its first dispatch; the AC has no path for an item the PRD assigns to another target, unlike FR-FLOW-212 AC-4 which records consent for a narrowed requirement scope.
findings.suggested_action: Let AC-2 exempt items the PRD (or the kiwi-srs verdict `other-wave`) assigns to another target, or require the user's recorded consent for each deferred item as FR-FLOW-212 AC-4 does, and state which output field carries that exemption.

evidence.detail: 50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:16568 (FR-NODE-247 AC-2): "SHALL refuse a path not tracked at HEAD with `files-not-grounded` under the FR-NODE-216 AC-6 rule" vs 30.cli-interface.srs.md:5222 (IR-CLI-084 AC-2, the rule FR-NODE-216 AC-6 applies): "An SDS Files path that does not exist and has no repository path within Levenshtein distance 2 is accepted and the plan is produced, so a unit that creates new files is not refused." Also 60.workflow-release.srs.md:13747 (FR-FLOW-195 AC-1): files[] is filled "from the wave's existing modules and expected new paths".

findings.description: AC-2 says every path not tracked at HEAD is refused, while the rule it invokes accepts a new path with no near neighbour; a test with an expected new file (which the impact analysis of FR-FLOW-212 AC-1 must be able to name) cannot satisfy both readings.
findings.suggested_action: Rewrite the clause to "SHALL ground each path by the FR-NODE-216 AC-6 rule (a near-miss of a tracked path is refused with `files-not-grounded`; a new path with no near neighbour is accepted)".

evidence.detail: 50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:16691 (FR-NODE-249 AC-1) makes an AC done "only WHEN ... at least one test cites" it and, when the scan did not run, only says the condition is "reported unchecked" with `cited_checked: false`; it never says whether such an AC counts as done. :16692 (AC-2) makes a `complete` node `done` only when every AC is done, else `unverified`. 30.cli-interface.srs.md:7055 (IR-CLI-113 AC-4) defers the unscanned case back to FR-NODE-249 AC-1. :16809 and :16811 (FR-NODE-251 AC-1, AC-3) give `wave actions` no scan option and no statement whether it scans, yet make an action due only for a `done` node (AC-4: `unverified` holds every action).

findings.description: For a completed node whose ACs are checked and covered, the expected state without the citation scan (done or unverified) is undefined, so a test of `wave status` without `--with-tests`, and of whether `wave actions` ever reports a notify as due, has no determinate expected output. Under the strict reading every completed node is `unverified` in default `wave status` and no completion action is ever due.
findings.suggested_action: State the unscanned outcome explicitly (for example: an AC whose only unknown is the citation counts as done-unchecked and does not make the node `unverified`), and state in FR-NODE-251 AC-1 whether `wave actions` runs the scan.

evidence.detail: 50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:16990 (FR-NODE-254 AC-1) fixes a round row as `{id, verdict, kept, evidence?}`; :16991 (AC-2) requires, under `--max`, "rows from two verifiers, a round with rows from one verifier returning `invalid`". Neither the row nor the existing `Round` input (src/core/orchestrator/verification-gate.ts:16-40: `RoundRow {id, verdict, severity}`, Round fields loop/scope/roundIndex/mode/cap/streakBefore/frozenDenominator/rows/fixAppliedThisRound/regression/residual) carries a verifier identity.

findings.description: evaluateRound cannot tell rows of one verifier from rows of two with the row shape AC-1 fixes, so the `--max` clause of AC-2 (and the FR-NODE-144 AC-5 mode difference the Implementation Notes rely on) is not testable.
findings.suggested_action: Add a verifier field to the row (e.g. `{id, verdict, kept, evidence?, verifier}`) or a per-round verifier count input, and say which one AC-2 reads.

evidence.detail: 60.workflow-release.srs.md:15088 (FR-FLOW-217 AC-1): "A remaining wave SHALL be a node with no `phase=\"worker\"` line in the run journal, read through `orchestrate wave status`". The fields `wave status` returns per node (30.cli-interface.srs.md:7052, IR-CLI-113 AC-1, plus IR-CLI-104 AC-1) are the latest line's `status`/`phase`/`ts` and derived `state`, `started_at` (first `in_progress`, FR-NODE-249 AC-3) — none records whether any `phase=worker` line exists. Counter-case: a re-entered node (`r{m}`) whose journal holds a worker line followed by a later `in_progress` line with `phase=schedule` shows only `phase: schedule`.

findings.description: The remaining-wave predicate is defined on journal content that the named reader does not expose, so a host following FR-FLOW-222 AC-5 (read progress only through `wave status`) cannot evaluate it, and a test of the predicate through `wave status` has no field to assert on.
findings.suggested_action: Either add a per-node `dispatched` (or `first_dispatched_at`) field to IR-CLI-113 AC-1, or define the remaining-wave predicate on fields `wave status` already returns.
